stem: A 26-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral valve disease has had 3 weeks of low fever and tiredness that began after a root canal. A new apical holosystolic murmur is heard. Blood cultures grow Gram-positive cocci in chains that are alpha-hemolytic, resistant to optochin and insoluble in bile.
oneliner: 26F + rheumatic mitral valve + 3 wk low fever after root canal + new murmur + GPC in chains, alpha-hemolytic, optochin resistant, bile insoluble → which organism?
ask: Which organism is most likely responsible?

options.B: Viridans group streptococci (S. mitis, S. sanguinis)

whyNot.A: Also alpha-hemolytic, but **optochin sensitive and bile soluble**
whyNot.D: **Gamma-hemolytic, grows in bile and 6.5% salt**; after GI or urinary procedures

why: **Subacute endocarditis on a damaged valve after dental work + alpha-hemolytic, optochin-resistant, bile-insoluble streptococci** = viridans group. Their **dextran** helps them stick to fibrin-platelet clumps on the valve.

bug.name: Viridans streptococci (S. mitis, S. sanguinis, S. mutans)
bug.type: Gram-positive cocci in chains, catalase negative
bug.virulence: Dextran binds fibrin-platelet aggregates on damaged valves
bug.spread: Normal mouth flora; enters blood with dental work
bug.causes: Subacute endocarditis on abnormal valves; dental caries (S. mutans)

stem: A 66-year-old man had a mechanical aortic valve placed 6 weeks ago. He now has fever, malaise and a new regurgitant murmur. Two sets of blood cultures grow gram-positive cocci in clusters. The isolate is catalase-positive and coagulase-negative, and it is not hemolytic.
oneliner: 66M + mechanical aortic valve 6 wk ago + fever + new regurgitant murmur + GPC in clusters, catalase +, coagulase − → which organism?
ask: Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

whyNot.B: Grow in **chains** and are **catalase-negative**; this isolate is clustered and catalase-positive
whyNot.D: **Catalase-negative** streptococci in chains; linked to colon cancer

why: **Fever, a new murmur and clustered gram-positive cocci** that are **catalase-positive and coagulase-negative** in a patient with a **prosthetic valve** point to **S. epidermidis**. It makes **biofilm** on foreign material and is the leading cause of early prosthetic valve infection.

bug.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
bug.lab: Catalase positive, coagulase negative, novobiocin sensitive (unlike S. saprophyticus)
bug.virulence: Polysaccharide biofilm on prosthetic material and catheters
bug.spread: Skin flora introduced at surgery or through indwelling devices
bug.causes: Prosthetic valve endocarditis (early), catheter and shunt infections, prosthetic joint infection

idea.rule: Skin flora that forms biofilm on foreign material causes device-related infection.
also: Cutibacterium acnes also forms biofilm on shoulder implants and shunts
